title: Async-FIFO Read Pointer (Gray)
constraints: The read side of an 8-entry asynchronous FIFO. It keeps a 4-bit binary read pointer (one extra bit) and publishes it as a **registered** Gray code `rd_gray`.
`wr_gray_sync` is the write pointer (Gray) already synchronized into this clock domain. `empty = (rd_gray == wr_gray_sync)` (combinational).
A rising edge with `rd_en && !empty` advances the pointer by one. `rd_addr` = the low 3 bits of the binary pointer. Synchronous reset → pointer 0.
hints: Keep `rd_bin` (4 bits). On a pop, register both `rd_bin + 1` and its Gray code `(n >> 1) ^ n`.
Comparing Gray codes for equality works directly: equal binary ⇔ equal Gray.
Why Gray? `rd_gray` crosses into the write domain through a 2-flop synchronizer, and a Gray count changes only one bit per step.

examples.title: wrap
examples.expected: Gray code wraps with one bit change
